---
title: "Figure 4—figure supplement (number pending) — does the interval you would quote contain the truth? Coverage of the nominal 95% region"
author: "Luciano Moffatt"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: html_document
---

<!--
NUMBER PENDING, as for the other rebuilt supplements.

WHAT IT IS, AND WHY IT IS NOT ANOTHER MAP. Every figure on the design plane reports a RATIO: how
far the reported second moment is from the delivered one. This one reports the thing a reader can
act on, which is a probability: if you ran this experiment and quoted the error bar your own fit
hands you, how often would the truth be inside it?

The statistic is the squared Mahalanobis distance of each fit from the TRUTH, in the metric of
that fit's OWN Fisher information:

    d2_k = (theta_hat_k - theta_true)' F_k (theta_hat_k - theta_true)

which is chi-squared with six degrees of freedom if the reported covariance is right. The
coverage plotted is the fraction of fits with d2_k below the 95th percentile of that reference.
Every fit in the cloud carries its own 6x6 Fisher, so this is not an aggregate standing in for an
experiment: it is the experiment, repeated.

TWO ROWS, AND THE GAP BETWEEN THEM IS THE BIAS. Row A centres on the truth, which is what a
confidence interval claims to contain, so it carries the bias and the variance together. Row B
centres on the cloud's own mean, which removes the bias by construction and leaves only the
question the plane figures ask. A member that sits at 0.95 in B and at zero in A is precisely
calibrated about the wrong point.

THE LINE TYPE IS HOW MUCH YOU POOL, and it is the axis this figure exists for. At group size 100
the estimate comes from a hundred recordings, so its standard error is ten times smaller than a
single recording's while any bias is exactly where it was. Pooling therefore buys precision and
spends coverage, and the two curves show the exchange rate. The cloud carries group sizes 10 and
100 at every cell, 1000 and 100 fits respectively, so a coverage carries about +-1.4 and +-2.2 per
cent of binomial error.

THE HORIZONTAL LINE IS 0.95 and it is the only reference that matters: a member on it is honest at
that design point, whatever its distortion says.

WHAT IT IS BUILT FROM. The MLE clouds at noise label 0.1, all seven acquisition intervals, the
four members that have them (INR has one cloud cell so far and is absent). CONVERGED FITS ONLY:
`Convergence_Status_Code` is emitted per fit and nothing in this project filtered on it until now.
It matters where the interval is short — in the highest-count cloud, 99 of 1000 fits at
Delta*k_off = 0.05 sat at the 100-iteration cap — and the fraction kept is printed per cell on the
render log.

theta_true is in no CSV and is written down in the code: in log10 of the natural units, k_on 10,
k_off 100, unitary current 1, baseline 1, N_ch the cell's, and the instrumental noise THE LABEL
OVER A THOUSAND. That last one is the trap this project documents, and getting it wrong shifts
sigma_noise by 0.3 in log10 and quietly ruins every distance.

LSE CARRIES ITS OWN TRUTH VECTOR AND ITS OWN DEGREES OF FREEDOM. nonlinearsqr indexes its own four
parameters and they do not line up with the macro ones: its index 2 is the baseline and its 3 is
the channel number, where the macro members have the unitary current and the noise scale. So its
d2 is over a FOUR-dimensional space against chi-squared with four degrees of freedom, and its
theta_true is written separately. The first render of this figure used the macro vector for it and
put LSE flat at zero in row A for a reason that had nothing to do with least squares. The
comparison across members is like for like as a probability and not as a distance, and the caption
has to say so.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
suppressMessages({ library(data.table); library(ggplot2) })
```

```{r data}
# ---- source data, built once and written as CSV, like the plane figures ------------------------
SRC <- "../figure_4_source_data/figure_4_source_data_coverage.csv"
ALGOS <- c(nonlinearsqr = "LSE", macro_NR = "NR", macro_R = "R", macro_IR = "IR")
NCHS  <- c(10, 100, 1000, 10000)
Z     <- "0.1"
.pre  <- function(a) if (a == "nonlinearsqr") "figure_3_LSE_" else "figure_3_G_"

cloud_file <- function(a, n) {
  f <- Sys.glob(file.path("../data", "*",
    sprintf("%snch_%d_nsim_10000_%s_noise_%s_mle_cloud_runs.csv", .pre(a), n, a, Z)))
  if (length(f)) f[1] else NA_character_
}

stamp <- local({
  fs <- na.omit(unlist(lapply(names(ALGOS), function(a) vapply(NCHS, function(n) cloud_file(a, n), ""))))
  i  <- file.info(c(fs, "figure_4_supplement_coverage.Rmd"))
  sprintf("# figure_4 coverage | clouds=%d bytes=%.0f newest=%.0f", length(fs),
          sum(i$size, na.rm = TRUE), max(as.numeric(i$mtime), na.rm = TRUE))
})

cover_cell <- function(a, n) {
  f <- cloud_file(a, n); if (is.na(f)) return(NULL)
  d <- fread(f, skip = 1, showProgress = FALSE)
  # theta_true PER MEMBER, because nonlinearsqr indexes its own four parameters and they do not
  # line up: its 2 is the baseline and its 3 is the channel number, where the macro members have
  # the unitary current and the noise scale. Read off `param_name` in the files. Using the macro
  # vector for LSE put its truth for N_ch at log10(noise/1000) and drove its coverage to zero for
  # a reason that had nothing to do with the algorithm.
  th0 <- if (a == "nonlinearsqr")
           c(`0` = 1, `1` = 2, `2` = 0, `3` = log10(n))
         else
           c(`0` = 1, `1` = 2, `2` = 0, `3` = log10(as.numeric(Z) / 1000), `4` = 0,
             `5` = log10(n))
  out <- list()
  for (gs in sort(unique(d$group_size))) for (dlt in sort(unique(d$interval_in_tau))) {
    cv <- d[variable == "Convergence_Status_Code" & group_size == gs & interval_in_tau == dlt]
    ok <- if (nrow(cv)) cv$sample_index[cv$value == 0] else NULL
    TH <- d[variable == "Model_Parameters_Hat" & group_size == gs & interval_in_tau == dlt &
            (is.null(ok) | sample_index %in% ok),
            .(sample_index, param_index, value)]
    if (!nrow(TH)) next
    nfit <- uniqueN(TH$sample_index); if (nfit < 20) next
    P <- uniqueN(TH$param_index)

    FI <- d[variable == "Gaussian_Fisher_Information" & group_size == gs &
            interval_in_tau == dlt & sample_index %in% TH$sample_index,
            .(sample_index, param_index, param_col, value)]

    for (centre in c("truth", "mean")) {
      ref <- if (centre == "truth") th0[as.character(sort(unique(TH$param_index)))] else
             TH[, mean(value), by = param_index][order(param_index)]$V1
      dv <- copy(TH)[, dev := value - ref[match(param_index, sort(unique(TH$param_index)))]]
      # d2 = sum_ij dev_i F_ij dev_j, as two joins instead of one matrix per fit
      z <- merge(FI, dv[, .(sample_index, param_index, di = dev)],
                 by = c("sample_index", "param_index"))
      z <- merge(z, dv[, .(sample_index, param_col = param_index, dj = dev)],
                 by = c("sample_index", "param_col"))
      d2 <- z[, sum(value * di * dj), by = sample_index]$V1
      out[[length(out) + 1]] <- data.table(
        algo = a, nch = n, gs = gs, dlt = dlt, centre = centre, p = P, nfit = nfit,
        conv = if (nrow(cv)) mean(cv$value == 0) else NA_real_,
        cover = mean(d2 <= qchisq(0.95, P), na.rm = TRUE))
    }
  }
  rbindlist(out)
}

fresh <- file.exists(SRC) && identical(readLines(SRC, n = 1), stamp)
if (fresh) {
  cat("coverage: source CSV is current, reading it\n")
  CV <- as.data.table(read.csv(SRC, skip = 1))
} else {
  cat("coverage: sweeping the clouds\n")
  CV <- rbindlist(lapply(names(ALGOS), function(a)
    rbindlist(lapply(NCHS, function(n) {
      r <- cover_cell(a, n)
      if (!is.null(r)) cat(sprintf("  %-14s N_ch %-6d fits %4d  converged %.2f\n",
                                   a, n, r$nfit[1], r$conv[1]))
      r
    }))))
  dir.create(dirname(SRC), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  writeLines(stamp, SRC)
  suppressWarnings(write.table(CV, SRC, sep = ",", row.names = FALSE, col.names = TRUE,
                               append = TRUE, qmethod = "double"))
}
CV[, lab := factor(ALGOS[algo], levels = unname(ALGOS))]
CV[, nchf := factor(sprintf("N[ch]==%d", nch), levels = sprintf("N[ch]==%d", NCHS))]
CV[, row := factor(ifelse(centre == "truth", "A~~centred~on~the~truth",
                          "B~~centred~on~the~cloud~mean"))]
```

```{r plot, fig.width = 7.0, fig.height = 4.4}
PAL <- c(LSE = "#7F7F7F", NR = "#D6604D", R = "#4393C3", IR = "#053061")
g <- ggplot(CV, aes(dlt, cover, colour = lab, linetype = factor(gs))) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.95, colour = "grey40", linewidth = .3) +
  geom_line(linewidth = .45) + geom_point(size = .7) +
  facet_grid(row ~ nchf, labeller = label_parsed) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(.01, .1, 1), labels = c("0.01", "0.1", "1")) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0, .5, .95),
                     labels = c("0", "0.5", "0.95")) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = PAL, name = NULL) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(`10` = "22", `100` = "solid"),
                        name = "recordings\npooled") +
  labs(x = expression(widetilde(Delta) == Delta %.% k[off]),
       y = "fraction of fits whose nominal 95% region contains the reference") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 8, base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "right",
        legend.key.size = unit(9, "pt"), strip.text = element_text(size = 7),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 8), axis.text = element_text(size = 7),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 7), legend.title = element_text(size = 7))
g
ggsave("Figure_4_supplement_coverage.pdf", g, width = 7.0, height = 4.4)
cat(sprintf("Figure_4_supplement_coverage.pdf: 7.00 x 4.40 in, %d cells\n",
            nrow(CV) / 2))
```

```{r numbers}
# the headline, as a table, so the caption never has to be read off the lines
knitr::kable(dcast(CV[centre == "truth" & abs(dlt - 1) < 1e-9], lab + gs ~ nch,
                   value.var = "cover"), digits = 3,
             caption = "coverage centred on the truth, Delta*k_off = 1")
knitr::kable(dcast(CV[centre == "mean" & abs(dlt - 1) < 1e-9], lab + gs ~ nch,
                   value.var = "cover"), digits = 3,
             caption = "the same, centred on the cloud mean")
```
